resolutions.rationale: This condition is a normative contradiction between two interface statements in the same package, not a missing premise or a defective input. S34 says StoreConfiguration is invoked once a configuration log entry is committed; S35 says ApplyBatch is sent LogConfiguration entries. The implementation cannot satisfy both for a FSM implementing both interfaces, because S36 shows the sole StoreConfiguration call site inside applySingle and S37 shows the batching dispatch never reaching applySingle. The answer fixes which written responsibility the check encodes - the explicit ConfigurationStore contract that the scenario's FSM implements - and preserves the competing ApplyBatch statement as a scope boundary instead of erasing it. The completed execution 41bb5656bcc7426dab29aae5e648536f corroborates that the two statements do not both hold for this FSM (store_configuration_calls 0 while indices [1,4] reached ApplyBatch).
scope_limitations: Whether ConfigurationStore is contractually limited to non-batching FSMs, or whether a FSM implementing both interfaces is an unsupported combination, stays open and is carried as a limitation of this review.

units.rationale: First Candidate, grounded on the accepted map. Reading the previously unmapped FSM/apply path (fsm.go) surfaced a sourced discrepancy: ConfigurationStore documents that StoreConfiguration is invoked once a configuration log entry is committed (configuration.go:38-52), but the only call site is inside applySingle, and runFSM calls applySingle only when the FSM does NOT implement BatchingFSM (fsm.go:127-186). Separately, BatchingFSM.ApplyBatch documents that LogConfiguration entries 'will be sent' to the batching FSM (fsm.go:51-69). A FSM that implements both interfaces therefore never receives StoreConfiguration, and the configuration fact is established for it only by whatever its own ApplyBatch chooses to do. The library's own test helper (testing_batch.go:13-33) implements ApplyBatch under the batchtest build flag and simply returns nil for non-LogCommand entries, which is consistent with the discrepancy rather than with the ConfigurationStore contract. This product therefore fixes the responsibility, the attribution and a bounded discriminator; construction of the formal check is deferred to the next turn. The map is extended with the behavior and fact that support this question (b-fsm-apply-committed, f-fsm-configuration-state); no previously accepted object is modified or removed.

audit_question.question: When a FSM implements both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore, does the library invoke StoreConfiguration(index, configuration) for a committed LogConfiguration entry, as the ConfigurationStore contract states, or does the batching dispatch in runFSM make that invocation unreachable?
audit_question.importance: ConfigurationStore exists so a persistent FSM can treat its own state as a complete snapshot and recover without an external snapshot (configuration.go:44-52). If the invocation is unreachable for batching FSMs, an application that implements both interfaces silently loses the only library-provided delivery of committed configuration changes, which matters for recovery and for the FSM's own view of cluster membership. This is an implementation/contract gap, not a consensus-safety violation; it is classified implementation_semantics.

selections.rationale: First, partial-but-usable core map for the hashicorp/raft snapshot (module github.com/hashicorp/raft, commit c0dc6a0b). The submission records the two core relationships required by the activity roles and, crucially, their connection, from read code plus the membership design document: (A1) qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement, realized as pre-vote campaign -> real vote campaign -> per-term vote grants -> leader no-op + replication -> quorum commitment at or above the first index of the leader's term; and (A2) context validity and acquisition/transfer/loss of authority, realized as the durable current term plus per-term vote, step-down-and-bump on newer terms, and leadership transfer via TimeoutNow with the candidateFromLeadershipTransfer exemption. The connection is sourced: formation eligibility and the commitment quorum are read from the latest configuration; configuration changes are only opened once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (configurationChangeChIfStable), which is why a no-op is always dispatched on election; and old work is bounded by present authority (votes honoured only for their own term, an AppendEntries reply reporting a newer term driving handleStaleTerm/step-down, conflicting-suffix truncation rolling latest back to committed, and inflight futures failed with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down). Residual local anomalies are recorded under core_overview.open_details rather than blocking the overview: the appendEntries StoreLogs-failure TODO leaving lastLog stale (raft.go:1541), electSelf returning a nil response channel on self-vote persistence failure (raft.go:2023), and checkLeaderLease assuming a replState entry exists for every latest-config voter (raft.go:1054). Several high-consequence paths remain explicitly unmapped surfaces (installSnapshot body, leader-side snapshot shipping, runFSM, snapshot lifecycle), and the next step is to read them and pick a sourced discriminator rather than to treat this map as coverage. No obligation or check is claimed here.

formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

after.meaning: The cluster configuration currently in effect (latest) and the configuration known to be committed, each with its log index.
after.validity_context: latest is in effect from the moment its log entry is appended; committed is the newest configuration whose entry has been committed. At most one uncommitted configuration exists at a time.

after.meaning: The leader's commitIndex: the highest index the leader holds to be committed because a quorum of voters store a matching log.
after.validity_context: Only meaningful for the term in which the leader is elected; advancing it requires the quorum match to be at least startIndex (the first entry of the leader's own term).
after.durability: Not durable on the leader; recomputed from match indexes; followers persist the same entries the leader has and learn the index from LeaderCommitIndex.
after.recovery: Recomputed from replication after an election; no persisted commit index is trusted on restart.

after.meaning: Per-server record that a server's durable log agrees with the leader through at least a given index.
after.validity_context: Derived from a successful local write or a successful AppendEntries reply (last entry index), and only tracked for voters of the configuration currently installed in the commitment struct.
after.recovery: Re-derived after a leader election as replication catches up.

resolution_basis.rationale: This condition is a normative contradiction between two interface statements in the same package, not a missing premise or a defective input. S34 says StoreConfiguration is invoked once a configuration log entry is committed; S35 says ApplyBatch is sent LogConfiguration entries. The implementation cannot satisfy both for a FSM implementing both interfaces, because S36 shows the sole StoreConfiguration call site inside applySingle and S37 shows the batching dispatch never reaching applySingle. The answer fixes which written responsibility the check encodes - the explicit ConfigurationStore contract that the scenario's FSM implements - and preserves the competing ApplyBatch statement as a scope boundary instead of erasing it. The completed execution 41bb5656bcc7426dab29aae5e648536f corroborates that the two statements do not both hold for this FSM (store_configuration_calls 0 while indices [1,4] reached ApplyBatch).
scope_limitations: Whether ConfigurationStore is contractually limited to non-batching FSMs, or whether a FSM implementing both interfaces is an unsupported combination, stays open and is carried as a limitation of this review.
